key_insight: Instead of compressing a pretrained model and then fine-tuning adapters sequentially, jointly learn compressed adapter subspaces that are aware of downstream tasks — forming a task-aware union of subspaces so compression and adaptation reinforce each other.
problem_solved: The common compress-then-adapt workflow can misalign the compressed parameter subspace with downstream objectives and waste global parameter budget, reducing task performance and efficiency.
method: Joint optimization: learn adapter parameters and their low-rank/compressed basis simultaneously rather than in sequence.
Task-aware union of subspaces: construct a shared union of task-specific low-dimensional subspaces that captures both common structure and task-specific directions.
Budget-aware allocation: dynamically allocate compressed capacity across tasks to maximize accuracy under a global parameter/compute constraint.
impact: JACTUS enables more accurate and parameter-efficient adaptation of large pretrained models by aligning compression with downstream objectives, improving the accuracy-vs-size tradeoff for practitioners using PEFT and model compression.
visual_elements: Pipeline comparison: side-by-side diagram contrasting sequential (compress → adapt) vs joint (compress+adapt) workflows.
Subspace illustration: 2D/3D diagram showing a union of task-specific low-dimensional subspaces inside a high-dimensional parameter space.
Budget vs performance chart: curve or scatter showing better accuracy for a given parameter budget with JACTUS compared to baseline compress-then-adapt.
Allocation heatmap: matrix or bar chart showing how compressed capacity is distributed across tasks under a shared budget.
paper_title: Compress Then Adapt? No, Do It Together via Task-aware Union of Subspaces
paper_authors: Jingze Ge, Yun Liu, Xue Geng, Wanqi Dong, Wang Zhe Mark
